title: Introduce priority backpressure simulator and cross-batch attribution reporter
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Motivation: Production workloads show that high-priority short bursts can create transient backpressure that amplifies latency for lower-priority models sharing the same serving pool. Existing bench scenarios exercise steady-state mixes but do not quantify cross-priority cascade effects or attribute tail amplification to specific batches/kernels. This PR introduces a simulator and reporter to quantify cross-batch/backpressure effects and provide actionable signals for routing and batching heuristics.

What this PR adds: 1) priority-backpressure scenario runner (benchlab/scenarios/priority_backpressure.go): simulates multiple model queues with configurable priority classes, burst profiles, and backpressure propagation rules (queue headblocking, preemption, soft-eviction). 2) cross-batch attribution reporter (benchlab/reporters/crossbatch_attribution.py): consumes scenario traces and outputs per-batch and per-kernel attribution for p50/p95/p99 deltas attributable to higher-priority interference. 3) occupancy census telemetry (benchlab/metrics/occupancy_census.proto + exporters): collects per-GPU occupancy and per-kernel busy/idle epochs for finer granularity of kernel-level contention. 4) CI bench job updates (scripts/ci/bench-suite.yml): new deterministic seed mode and a perf-smoke stage. 5) docs and runbook (docs/bench/priority-backpressure.md) with instructions, recommended thresholds, and mitigation playbooks.

Design notes: - Simulator models both synchronous batching and continuous batching pipelines; it supports KV cache warm/cold starts and optional priming behavior. - Attribution reporter uses event-aligned difference-in-paths: it constructs cohorts of high-priority bursts and compares tail quantiles of co-located low-priority cohorts after aligning warmup windows; output includes JSON per-run and a compact Prometheus-compatible metrics export. - Config-driven: any bench scenario can be augmented with a priority-tier definition and backpressure policy to test rollout strategies.

Checklist: - [x] New scenario implementation with unit tests and deterministic seed. - [x] Reporter outputs validated against synthetic traces. - [x] CI bench-suite updated to include a fast-smoke run. - [x] Docs and runbook added. - [x] Performance regression guard added (bench-suite will fail PRs with >15% p99 regression unless opt-in).

How to run locally: ./benchlab run --scenario priority-backpressure --config ./benchlab/configs/priority_backpressure.yaml --out ./artifacts/pb_run.json

Expected outputs: - artifacts/pb_run.json (detailed trace + cohort attribution) - prometheus endpoint /metrics exposing bench_priority_backpressure_{p50,p95,p99}_delta and occupancy_census_{kernel}_{epoch} metrics.

Risk and mitigation: The new reporter runs offline and does not change serving code paths. The simulator is isolated to the bench harness but exercises code paths similar to our runtime; we added a safeguard to avoid any live cluster calls.

Related: ENG-7812 (routing policy experiments), ENG-7920 (KV cache warmup heuristics), SUP-1345 (customer incident analysis that motivated this work).

release_notes:
- Add 'priority-backpressure' benchmark scenario to benchlab for quantifying cross-priority interference and tail amplification.
- New cross-batch attribution reporter that produces per-batch kernel attribution and Prometheus metrics.
- Occupancy census telemetry for kernel-level contention analysis.
- Documentation and runbook with mitigation recommendations (routing rules, preemption, batching adjustments).
notes: This PR aims to make it easier for SREs and runtime engineers to reason about priority-induced tail effects and to test routing/quantization mitigations in the lab before rolling them to Dedicated/Private deployments. Follow-up work: automate cohort-based alerting and integrate with Optimize recommendations.
